composableIDModelR

composableIDModelR is an R interface to ComposableTuringIDModels.jl, the composable probabilistic infectious disease modelling package of the EpiAware ecosystem. You build a model in R from interchangeable latent process, infection and observation components, and Julia simulates from it and fits it with Turing.jl. You do not need to write any Julia, and as_julia() shows the Julia code that builds a model.

Installation

composableIDModelR needs Julia 1.12 or later. We recommend installing Julia with juliaup, which lets composableIDModelR use the Julia version its pinned dependencies were resolved with.

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("sbfnk/composableIDModelR")

The Julia packages install on first use. To install them up front and watch the progress, run:

library(composableIDModelR)
cidm_setup_julia()

Quick start

Estimate the reproduction number from COVID-19 cases in South Korea, following Mishra et al. (2020): an AR(2) process on log RtR_t drives a renewal model, observed with negative binomial noise.

library(composableIDModelR)

cases <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "south_korea_data.csv",
                              package = "composableIDModelR"))[45:80, ]

renewal <- Renewal(
  generation_time = Gamma(shape = 6.5, scale = 0.62),
  rt = AR(
    damp = list(truncated(Normal(0.8, 0.05), 0, 1),
                truncated(Normal(0.1, 0.05), 0, 1)),
    init = list(Normal(0, 0.2), Normal(0, 0.2)),
    epsilon_t = HierarchicalNormal(std = HalfNormal(0.1))
  ),
  initialisation = Normal(log(1), 0.1)
)
model <- IDModel(
  renewal,
  NegativeBinomialError(cluster_factor = HalfNormal(0.1))
)

fitted <- fit(model, cases$cases_new, dates = as.Date(cases$date))
fitted
summary(fitted)
plot(fitted, type = "Rt")
plot(fitted, type = "cases", horizon = 14)

To change an assumption, swap the component that encodes it. This model observes the same infections with Poisson noise after a reporting delay:

delayed <- IDModel(
  renewal,
  LatentDelay(PoissonError(), delay = LogNormal(1.6, 0.42))
)

component() calls any Julia constructor that has no R wrapper, and julia() inserts other Julia code, such as a function, verbatim.
